name: EtherVote
title: The Ghost of Spurious Dragon
tagline: Alex Van de Sande redeployed the old EtherVote contract on a quiet July day.

chapters.heading: The ghost of the vote
paragraphs: Marigolds scent the air as we remember EtherVote. It was born on July 10, 2017. A wallet ending in 9adb brought it into the world. On the day it was born it was written into a block, one page of Ethereum's shared record book.
The contract is a small program that lives on Ethereum. It arrived during the Spurious Dragon era. It was written in Solidity 0.4.11. Now it sits quiet, nearly 9.3 years old.

chapters.heading: The twin of the old vote
paragraphs: The contract sits like a shadow of a previous ghost. It came from the same source text and the same account as its predecessor. It appeared one year later to perform the same single task. It took a proposal hash and a yes or no choice, then let the choice go.

The compiler changed the way it was born. A 0.4 series release gave it a non payable check instead of a handwritten guard. It carried a 43 byte metadata trailer that the old versions did not have. It was last busy in 2017. It saw only 1 transaction in its life.

chapters.heading: The silence of EtherVote
paragraphs: The candle flickers over EtherVote. Its last call came on July 10, 2017. The vote function fell silent then.
It has been quiet for 9.3 years. The code still rests on the chain. It holds 0.0 ETH inside.
